The text carries the bytes SENT (`Buffer.byteLength(rendered.body, 'utf8')`), the cap of the surface written to (`WRITE_SURFACES`: comment → `COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT`, body → `ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT`), the overage and `SIZE_REMEDY`; `ROUTE_REMEDY` is its own constant and stays in exit 3's text only, pinned apart in both directions. Only the write path classifies (the pre-read keeps its PREREQUISITE reading). A refusal the cap does not explain (sent ≤ cap) says so and asks for a re-measurement instead of printing a zero overage — the reading that must move is the cap. `rest()` now attaches the platform's sentence (`platformRefusalText`: message + errors[].message) to every non-2xx error and exit 3's text prints it when present — the same defect family, mechanically part of the change, ⛔ no widening of exit 3's trigger. The regex is tested in place (`.test` on the declared non-global constant), which is exactly what the dev's first ablation caught: a copy rebuilt from `.source` with the flags retyped had made the declared `i` vacuous (fixed in `36ba41a64`; the pins made to fail by name in `290acfad0`).

The dispatch's unmeasured item ② is answered yes; item ① is measured: the two spellings differ in case (`Body` / `body`), hence the `i` flag; and the dispatch's naming of `PATCH /issues/comments/{id}` as a post-stamped surface was the seat's error — the tool writes `POST /issues/{n}/comments` and `PATCH /issues/{n}` only. The seat records that correction as its own.
- Seat spot-check on a scratch worktree at this head: `post-stamped.mjs --self-test` exit 0, 402 cases / 14 batteries (the dev's before: 349 / 13; the new battery floors at 53); `check-half-states.mjs --self-test` exit 0, 4,978 cases, 'ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT measured cap' 55 / 52 (was 40 / 37: +15 pins, the floor raised by exactly the cases added). The dev's four ablations are on the PR body with on-disk proof; the seat did not re-run them (the pins they exercise ran in the self-tests above).
